title: Lamb Biryani
subtitle: Slow-cooked lamb layered with saffron-infused basmati
excerpt: Spiced lamb slow-braised in yoghurt, then layered with saffron-tinted basmati rice and steamed together in a sealed pot until the rice absorbs the meat's flavours. The dum method gives a dish that is far more than the sum of its parts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Biryani is a Persian-origin dish that arrived in the Indian subcontinent with the Mughal Empire in the sixteenth century. The dum method, in which the rice and meat are sealed in a pot and steamed over a low heat, was developed by Mughal court cooks. Different regional styles have evolved across the subcontinent: Hyderabadi, Lucknawi (Awadhi), Kolkata, and Malabar are among the best-known. The British-Indian restaurant version tends to be a simplified rice dish rather than the full dum technique.

recipeTools.notes: Heavy pot with a tight-fitting lid, for the dum steaming.

content.text: Biryani takes a few hours but the method is not hard. Par-cook the rice to about 70 percent done, then layer it over the braised lamb. Seal the pot and let the steam finish the rice. The saffron goes into warm milk and is drizzled over just the top layer before sealing. Open the pot at the table and you will see gold threads running through the white rice.

items.preparation: soaked in cold water for 30 minutes

content.text: Fry the onions in 3 tablespoons of ghee over medium heat for 20 minutes until deep golden brown. Remove half to drain on kitchen paper for garnish. In the remaining onion and ghee, cook the garlic and ginger for 2 minutes. Add all the spices except saffron and stir for 1 minute. Add the yoghurt a tablespoon at a time, stirring between each. Add the lamb, salt, and 100 ml water. Cover and braise on a very low heat for 1 hour until tender. The sauce should be fairly thick.

Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil. Drain the soaked rice and add to the boiling water. Par-cook for exactly 5 minutes. The rice should be cooked on the outside but hard at the centre. Drain immediately.

Assemble: spoon the lamb and its sauce into the base of a heavy pot. Scatter half the fresh coriander and mint. Add the par-cooked rice in a layer. Drizzle the saffron milk over the rice. Top with the remaining coriander, mint, and fried onion. Add the remaining tablespoon of ghee.

Seal the pot tightly with foil, then press the lid on top. Cook over the lowest possible heat for 30 minutes. Remove from the heat and rest for 10 minutes before opening. Serve by digging down through all the layers.
